title: What Is the Best Farm Planning App for Small Rice Farmers in the Philippines?
metaTitle: Farm Planning App for Rice Farmers: What to Look For
metaDescription: Choosing a farm planning app for a small palay farm? Use these 8 checks, see how anee.io meets them, what it costs in pesos, and where it falls short.
excerpt: The best farm planning app for a small rice farm in the Philippines dates every task from your own transplanting or sowing day. It also knows the growth stages of palay, puts the weather beside the plan, works on an ordinary phone and costs little in pesos. anee.io, a farm app built for Filipino farmers, does all of this, and its Libre plan is free. Use it together with free government tools such as the Rice Crop Manager and the Binhing Palay app, because they answer different questions.

blocks.text: On a family palay farm, the farmer is also the manager, the bookkeeper and often the sprayer. A plan on paper gets wet, and a plan in your head forgets the second top dressing. So the app should carry the season for you, without a computer or a big monthly fee. Below are the checks to use before you pay, then an honest look at how anee.io meets them.

items: Pick an app that dates tasks by days after transplanting (DAT) or sowing (DAS) for each lot, not one fixed calendar for the whole farm.
It should know palay growth stages and show the forecast beside the plan, so a top dressing or a spray does not land on the day before rain.
It must run on the phone you already have, keep working where the signal is weak, and answer you in Tagalog or English.
anee.io meets these checks and starts free. Paid plans run from PHP 70 to PHP 600 a month, paid from any bank or wallet app.

blocks.text: Why counting days beats a wall calendar

Good rice practice ties the work to days after transplanting. For example, replant missing hills within 7 DAT and control weeds from 0 to 45 DAT. A farm planning app that counts DAT for each lot turns those rules into real dates on your phone.

blocks.text: How does anee.io turn a rice plan into dates?

items.title: Add your lots
items.text: Enter each field as a lot with its variety and size. Then mark the transplanting or sowing task as day zero.

items.title: Write or import the plan
items.text: Use the [Protocol Builder](/features/protocol-builder) to put each task on its DAT, with materials and rates. Or ask Anee for a Crop Protocol Analysis, which uses credits.

items.title: Let the calendar date it
items.text: The [cropping calendar](/features/cropping-calendar) places every task on the right day for each lot. Drag a task when rain moves your plan, and undo still works after you log out.

items.title: Follow the stage and the sky
items.text: Each day the board shows the lot's growth stage and the forecast. If a lot runs behind, set its delay counter.

items.title: Tick, record and report
items.text: Tick tasks done and mark who worked. After harvest, write the yield, price and buyer, and the reports add up the season.

blocks.title: Plan inside your irrigation schedule
blocks.text: Plant within 14 days before or after the regular schedule of your irrigation service area, after the field rests for at least 30 days. So put your area's schedule into the plan first, then build the season around it. A lot planted far from the others gives pests a longer meal.

blocks.text: Which free government tools should you use alongside an app?
Some questions are better answered by free government tools.

items: **Rice Crop Manager Advisory Service (RCMAS):** free crop and nutrient advice for your own field, run through DA offices and extension workers.
**Binhing Palay app:** a catalogue of released rice varieties, filtered by location, environment and season. It works offline.
**MOET App:** works with the MOET kit to give the amount, combination and type of fertilizer.
**PAGASA Agri Weather:** farm weather forecasts, ten day regional outlooks and tropical cyclone warnings for agriculture.

blocks.text: Then bring their answers into your plan. For example, put the RCMAS fertilizer rates into your Protocol Builder tasks, and type the variety you chose into the lot. Our guide to [fertilizer for rice](/blog/fertilizer-for-rice) shows the usual timings, and [pagtatanim ng palay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-palay) covers the whole crop.

items: Anee needs internet and uses credits. The board keeps working offline, but her answers and analyses wait for a signal.
Libre covers one active season with one lot, two days of weather and a few ads.
Workers, inventory and all the reports start at Solo Farmer. Worker logins and the Collab Room need Farm Owner.
It plans and keeps records, but it is not a soil laboratory. A soil test or MOET still tells you what your soil lacks.

blocks.text: Questions about choosing a farm planning app

items.q: Is there a free farm planning app for rice farmers in the Philippines?
items.a: Yes. anee.io has a free Libre plan with one active season, one lot, the activities board, growth stages and two days of weather, with a few ads. Free government tools such as the Binhing Palay app and the Rice Crop Manager Advisory Service also help with varieties and fertilizer.

items.q: Can I use a farm planning app without internet in the field?
items.a: anee.io keeps working without signal on every plan. Your ticks and notes wait on the phone and sync once the signal returns. Anee's chat and analyses need a connection.

items.q: Does the app work in Tagalog?
items.a: Yes. Anee, the smart farm technician inside anee.io, answers in Tagalog, Bisaya, Ilocano, Taglish or English. You can also send her a photo of a sick plant and ask in your own words.

items.q: Do I need a computer to use it?
items.a: No. anee.io runs in the browser of any phone, tablet or computer, and you can add it to your home screen.

items.q: Will a farm planning app raise my yield?
items.a: No app can promise a harvest. It helps you do the right work on the right day and keep records, so you see what to change next season. Your yield still depends on the variety, soil, water, weather and management.
